summary.en: Afghan Taliban mortar fire on the northwest Pakistan border killed one civilian and wounded five, while separate Afghan firing near Angoor Adda injured five people. Pakistan responded by striking Taliban positions, destroying border check posts, and launching an operation against illegal Afghans in Peshawar. The Pakistani minister linked the border closure to rising LPG prices, and arrest warrants were issued in the Radio Pakistan attack case. 1,794 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Afghanske Taliban-mortarild på den nordvestlige Pakistan-grensen drepte en sivil og såret fem, mens separat afghansk ildtreff nær Angoor Adda såret fem personer. Pakistan svarte med å angripe Taliban-posisjoner, ødelegge grensekontrollposter og iverksette en operasjon mot ulovlige afghanere i Peshawar. Den pakistanske ministeren knyttet grenselukningen til stigende LPG-priser, og arrestordre ble utstedt i saken om angrepet på Radio Pakistan. 1 794 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
